utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Case number IT-95-9-T, the Prosecutor versus Blagoje Simic, Miroslav Tadic, and Simo Zaric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Lukic. Cross-examination is continuing.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to all the participants in the proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Mrs. Bobic. Mrs. Bobic, I promised that I will be asking you questions for ten minutes, and I would like to be able to go through all my questions as fast as possible and to conclude your examination. We started discussing your exchange and the procedure of the exchange of you and your family. On page 47, line 8 of the transcript, you described how a courier came, five or six days before you went to be exchanged, and you started for the exchange on the 24th of December, 1993. And he told you to get ready, that you would be exchanged. Do you perhaps remember the name of the courier? Did you know that man?

utterances.speaker: EDIBA BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, I couldn't tell you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You also said yesterday that on the list that the courier brought, your husband's name was not there. Do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: EDIBA BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But he said that he would be picked up at Batkovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was the courier perhaps Stevan Tesic [As interpreted]? Do you know that man?

utterances.speaker: EDIBA BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: First you said that you didn't know him.

utterances.speaker: EDIBA BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Just a minute. I know that man, but I can't remember his name, because it was a long time ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Reidy.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honour, the transcript is completely ambiguous, Mr. Lukic's question at line 5 is: "Was the courier perhaps Stevan Tesic? Do you know that man?" And Mrs. Bobic answers yes. That's not clear whether the courier was Stevan Tesic or whether she knows Stevan Tesic or anything. I left that to see if counsel would clarify, but then, you know, counsel has tried to pick her up on that and says: "First you said you didn't know him." And that's, as you can see from the transcript, actually what she said, she didn't know the courier's name. She said, yes, she knew Stevan Tesic and it's not clear --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right, Ms. Reidy. Perhaps the witness can be allowed to explain the response.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First of all, we have to clarify, because the transcript is not correct. This is the man by the name of Stevan Tesic -- Stojan Tesic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is that the man who came to tell you that you would be exchanged and that Kemal would be picked up at Batkovici?

utterances.speaker: EDIBA BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That man came and he said that Kemal would be brought in for the exchange from Batkovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And that man's name is Stojan Tesic?

utterances.speaker: EDIBA BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On that occasion, as you said, he showed you a list without Kemal's name on it?

utterances.speaker: EDIBA BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This man Stojan was not a courier. He was there on behalf of the Red Cross, and he said that Kemal would be brought in. The courier was another man. That was the man who brought the list. This is the man whose name I cannot recall. It's been a really long time, and this is a very difficult subject.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let me go back to your interview with the Prosecution in May this year. In paragraph 74, you describe the arrival of the courier?

utterances.speaker: EDIBA BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The Prosecutor interpreted your words as follows: "He said -- he brought a new list under number 50. There were Ediba and Kemal, with his -- with their family, and number 51, there was Amira Bobic and her household."

utterances.speaker: EDIBA BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you the question. Did you tell the Prosecutor that under number 50 on that list that the courier had brought you --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have an objection from the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Ms. Reidy.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Yes. It may be a minor issue, but in the statement that I'm reading from, the paragraph does not refer to a new list, and that's what Mr. Lukic has quoted at paragraph 16. It says that, "It was after 6.00. I had finished forced labour for the day. He brought a list, and at number 50 it had Ediba and Kemal and family." So there was no new list, and in case there's any implication that some --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Which statement are you looking at, Ms. Reidy?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Well, the statement that Mr. Lukic said he was quoting from, which is the draft statement taken in May of this year.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would kindly like that this time not be counted as my ten minutes. I will now read from the draft version of the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's page 12 in the English version, paragraph 74. I'm reading. [In English] "And 50 it had Ediba and Kemal and family and at 51 was Almira Bobic and her husband."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The statement you have is the English one. Ms. Reidy?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: I have absolutely no qualms with that at all. That wasn't the point I was making. As I said, the paragraph does not refer to a new list. It just refers to the courier bringing a list, and that's what maybe -- can Mr. Lukic look at his draft statement, the paragraph he's just quoted from, and say that the courier brought a list, not a new list.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't understand what the Prosecutor is saying. I'm quoting from paragraph 74, where it says that the courier brought a new list. I'm reading from the statement that we had been given by the Prosecution, but I don't want to dwell on that. My question to the witness -- I can read again what is written in the document submitted to by the Prosecution. I have [In English] a new list, and at 50 it has Ediba and Kemal and family, and at 51 was Almira Bobic and her husband." [Interpretation] It says "new list."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic. We'll accept that your version says "a new list." I don't understand why there's differences, if it's a copy of the same document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Bobic, did you tell the Prosecutor that you had seen a list with the name of your husband on it? That's my question.

utterances.speaker: EDIBA BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My husband's name was not on the list, and the name of my sister's husband was also not on the list because he had died a few years before that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you whether that's what you stated to the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: EDIBA BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I said, and that's how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You claim that you stated --

utterances.speaker: EDIBA BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can I just clarify the situation? Because I can see that you cannot get the clear picture. After the meeting with Miro Brko, I had to go to the Red Cross to be entered on the list. When I was entered on the list, on it, under number 50, was Ediba Bobic and son Bedrudin, and it said that Kemal would come in from Batkovici. Under number 51, it says Almira, Nermina Bobic, Bedrija Arapovic Bobic, and Selma Arapovic. These are the family members that were on the list that was to be used during the exchange. But when I came, we did all that, and we were supposed to be exchanged. We had to be exchanged in the morning, at 7.00 a.m.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You told us all about that.

utterances.speaker: EDIBA BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to finish. Please let me finish.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No. No, please just answer my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... Allow the witness to complete what she is explaining, because the record won't be -- won't make sense. And Ms. Bobic, please, when counsel asks you to stop, please do listen to counsel, because you're supposed to be answering the questions put to you by counsel. Can we proceed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, the morning came. We came to the place where we were supposed to board the buses. We waited a long time for the buses. We got into the premises and the search lasted for a long time. I asked why my husband was not there, and Mr. Miro told me that we would meet at Dragalic. And when they came to Dragalic, we didn't meet him there either. When we crossed the border to Croatia, he wasn't there either. And from then on, I had to initiate proceedings to verify why Mr. Miro did not carry out what he had promised, because a promise is one thing and a lie is another thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you: What kind of proceedings did you have to initiate?

utterances.speaker: EDIBA BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well I gave a statement, I had to say that Mr. Miro did not want to exchange my husband.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was that the reason why you gave the statement?

utterances.speaker: EDIBA BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, had he made sure that my husband was exchanged, I would never have said that I had given him the money. But he did not do his job conscientiously, and that's why I did it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Bobic, you said that Stojan Tesic came to your apartment and told you that your husband would be brought for the exchange the same day when you were exchanged?

utterances.speaker: EDIBA BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Somebody sent him there. I don't know who it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Please tell me: Yesterday you said that Tadic searched everybody's bags?

utterances.speaker: EDIBA BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the pensioners' hall, before going to be exchanged?

utterances.speaker: EDIBA BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You said that when you boarded the buses, you saw that the bus with the people from Zasavica had already come in?

utterances.speaker: EDIBA BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was another bus.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And it arrived there in front of the pensioners' hall?

utterances.speaker: EDIBA BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Bobic, do you know Hajrija Drljacic?

utterances.speaker: EDIBA BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, she was a neighbour of mine, so I do know her. At the time she was a neighbour of mine. She lived close by to the hamburger stand where I worked.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know Teufik, her brother?

utterances.speaker: EDIBA BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know him from Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that they were exchanged on the same day as you were, together with the 87 people?

utterances.speaker: EDIBA BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's possible that we left together.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You told the Prosecutor that you remember very well that 87 of you were exchanged, and now I'm asking you, since you are so sure about this number: Do you remember having seen Hajrija Drljacic and her brother with you?

utterances.speaker: EDIBA BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me tell you: When we left from the station in front of the pensioners' hall -- please believe me that when we came to the graveyard and when I turned my head in that direction, and when I saw my child's grave, there was nothing I could see any more, and any time I look at that, I cannot get a clear picture of the event, because these are the events that cannot be expressed. This is something that one cannot explain, and you cannot explain how it came about that one was expelled from one's home and that one is unable to go back and live in one's hometown.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: We are not going into that. Please stick to the questions that counsel is asking you. We are all aware that you are very upset by recalling all of these events and you suffered a tragedy in the process of what we are trying to ask of you. But we are conducting a criminal trial, and we need the evidence to be on record. If you cannot remember the events clearly as to who was there, who was exchanged with you, you simply say that. We appreciate that it's a long time ago. We appreciate the circumstances of your family, but please do give answers to counsel. If you cannot remember, you say so. Can we proceed? Very well, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will move on to another topic. I've concluded the topic of the exchange.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Bobic, I will be asking you a few questions about what you testified yesterday about Mr. Cvijetin Stjepanovic [As interpreted].

utterances.speaker: EDIBA BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Stevanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Stevanovic. You described yesterday, on page 40, how you visited your husband, together with Cvijetin, and that he asked Kemal to sign a document, leaving all his property to him. Do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: EDIBA BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you see, when your husband signed this document for Mr. Stevanovic?

utterances.speaker: EDIBA BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see that, but I saw it when we met in Orasje, because my husband had brought this document with me, and he will show it to you when he comes here to testify.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So he didn't sign this document when you were there with Cvijetin?

utterances.speaker: EDIBA BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was there, but I was removed from the office, from the room. It wasn't an office, in fact. It wasn't a shed. I can't tell you what that place was. It was like a receptionist's room at the entrance gate where the ramp was. A woman from Bijeljina was there. She was present, because she handed the documents to him for his signature. She will tell you what was going on at that time, on that occasion. I told you all that I did before this document was signed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just answer me briefly: Were you in a position to speak to your husband for 45 minutes at that time? That's what you stated.

utterances.speaker: EDIBA BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We had it in writing that we were allowed to remain there for 45 minutes, and in the course of the 45 minutes, Cvijetin had a woman with him. I didn't know who she was, but she was a lawyer, in fact, and she had to speak to Kemal. And I had to leave the room and stay with the receptionist while they did that. They signed it, and that was when my husband and I had the opportunity to say hello. I'm telling you the truth, because this is something that I went through.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So you just said hello and then you said goodbye?

utterances.speaker: EDIBA BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We spoke, but there were two police officers who had brought Kemal to this receptionist's area, and he didn't know their names, but you will find that out from him.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the very same statement, the Prosecutor stated that, in paragraph 55, you said that: "First Cvijetin talked to Kemal to get to know him. He didn't know him. I then spoke with Kemal for 45 minutes." Did you state that to the Prosecution or not? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, it's paragraph 54.

utterances.speaker: EDIBA BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there must be a mistake in interpretation. We didn't have that long to talk. Cvijetin came there to actually get to know him, because he had to conduct the appropriate proceedings in Samac, appropriate paperwork to get our property.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So it wasn't like this, as this is described here?

utterances.speaker: EDIBA BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's possible that the interpretation was not right. People sometimes do not interpret my words correctly. I speak Bosnian. I do speak some English and some Croatian. So that sometimes the names are not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have a correction for the transcript. Page 10, line 11 -- page 10, line 19. I just wanted to correct that it says: "And then I spoke with Kemal."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In your statement in 1995, you had never mentioned the name of Cvijetin Stevanovic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EDIBA BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your question? I didn't understand you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will have to make a correction. I will read for the transcript what is entered in paragraph 54 of the statement, dated 18th of May this year: "I then spoke with Kemal for 45 minutes." And now I will ask my next question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you mention Cvijetin in your interview with the Prosecution in 1995? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: EDIBA BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't know that until my husband brought in the document. I didn't know that this was the way that it had been done.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You probably know that your husband spoke with the Prosecutors in 1998?

utterances.speaker: EDIBA BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, possibly. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your husband told you about what he spoke about with the Prosecution, and he said that he didn't mention Cvijetin Stevanovic?

utterances.speaker: EDIBA BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you: We didn't have the document with which we started this process. We did it in Brcko, and the process was completed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay. We'll learn that from your husband. Do you know that this paper that your husband signed is, in fact, the power of attorney authorising Cvijetin Stevanovic that he is entitled to use your property but that he cannot sell it without the express approval of your husband, and that if he should sell it, he should give the money to your husband? Do you know that? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: EDIBA BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says "until revoked." That means that the moment we show up, that it no longer is valid. I'm sure that this was done by the lady lawyer, that she did it right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But you confirm that you remained in your apartment until the time when you were exchanged?

utterances.speaker: EDIBA BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was just a very brief time while he was taking out and carrying away all the stuff.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Am I right, Mrs. Bobic, when I say that you and your husband decided to mention Cvijetin before this Trial Chamber only in 2002 because that was the time that you had a lawsuit against him before the local court?

utterances.speaker: EDIBA BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Do you know why I mentioned that in this year? Because when -- through IPTF and through the authorities, I sought to prove with this document that we had in our hands, we had to notify IPTF to tell them what Cvijetin had done before we had left Bosanski Samac. The IPTF took this paper and they conducted their proceedings, and they said that Kemal or I had to come to Pelagicevo, to go to Cvijetin's house, to be able to talk to him, and so that Cvijetin would then return our property to us. However, in that period when I went to Pelagicevo, I'm sure that he had very, very good friends that he worked with. Those were the paramilitaries. At the time when I came there, the situation was not really clear. It was not really easy to get into the Republika Srpska. You know that very well, especially in Pelagicevo and Loncari. At that time, I entered Pelagicevo once. Little Miso, from Bosanski Samac, worked there and he received me quite well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let us not go into that.

utterances.speaker: EDIBA BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Please let me finish my thoughts. Let me express my thoughts. Everything went fine then, and after the third -- second or third --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... saying. If there is need for any explanation, the Prosecution will ask you to explain when their turn comes to re-examine you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You will be able to answer all the questions that the Prosecution will ask you. Now please answer my questions. I hope you understand what the Trial Chamber has told you. Did you, as early as in 1993, initiate proceedings for the return of your property?

utterances.speaker: EDIBA BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know that your husband and your sister, who are co-owners of your property, did, as early as July 1993, give some of your real estate to Gordana Pavlovic, the girlfriend of your late son? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: EDIBA BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So they never gave anything to Gordana Pavlovic as a gift?

utterances.speaker: EDIBA BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I have just a few questions, Your Honours, but I would now like to go into private session, because I will be asking questions about some witnesses who are protected.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well. We'll go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Bobic, just one more question: You described how you were in a bus when you were exchanged. Is it true that from the pensioners' hall, the bus passed Mebos on its way to Crkvina, did not pass the Muslim graveyard?

utterances.speaker: EDIBA BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It did pass the Muslim graveyard. That was the most difficult moment for me, having to leave the graves behind me. This was my hearth, the place where I lived. I can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Calm down. Mr. Lukic, was that necessary, the question that it passed wherever it passed?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I think that these are some facts that are very important, what this witness said about my client, these facts are very important and very serious, and during my cross-examination I did not ask a single question regarding this witness's son. However, I have facts and I have information, and if the witness touched upon that, then I think it's very important to bring out the claim of my client, which is that the bus never passed by the graveyard.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It did. It did pass.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. Lukic. Are you through?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I've finished with my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I have to check with the registry at one stage where we have to open the record. Because, as Mr. Lukic said, he didn't require private session. So we have to check that. Ms. Reidy?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honour, could I just ask for a five-minute recess? I think it will make the next proceedings go more quickly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. We'll have a recess to allow the witness to calm down. --- Break taken at 9.36 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Before we proceed, Ms. Reidy, I just want to correct the record. The record should be open as from page 14, line 11. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mrs. Bobic, before we start, just because I'm going to ask you a few questions about matters put to you by Defence counsel, I'd like you just to be shown the statement that Defence counsel has quoted you from. It's your statement from the 14th of February, 1995. And I'm going to show you the English version of the copy, just because that's the one upon which your signature appears.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: So can I just ask if the usher could show that document to the witness?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Ms. Reidy, sorry to interrupt you. I've been advised by the registry assistant that the correct -- the correction should be -- the record should be open from page 15, line 8, at 0930 hours. Because we went along with private session, but it should be open as at that time, page 15, line 8.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mrs. Bobic, the only thing I want you to do is to look at that document and see if that's your signature at the bottom of that document and on the subsequent pages.

utterances.speaker: EDIBA BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mrs. Bobic, is the document you have in front of you - it's in the English language; that's right?

utterances.speaker: EDIBA BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And am I correct that in fact what it amounts to is actually three pages of -- three and a little bit pages of information? Well, let me -- in total, the document is six pages; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EDIBA BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Six.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And the first and the last page are kind of forms that just give standard information?

utterances.speaker: EDIBA BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And the middle there's about three and a half pages of information you provided to investigators in 1995; is that right?

utterances.speaker: EDIBA BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. Perhaps you can give it back to the usher. It's in English, so you won't be able to read it, but if the Defence counsel want to check it's the same document they have, they can. So that's your statement in 1995. Now, Defence counsel have also asked you questions about a statement that was recorded this year, indeed by myself, and you had a look at that draft statement when you came here, and it's about 16 pages long; is that correct? It's a much longer statement than the one you gave in 1995.

utterances.speaker: EDIBA BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. So there were a lot of questions asked in 2002 that perhaps the investigator in 1995 didn't put to you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EDIBA BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour. Can you give me one second? I seem to have misplaced --

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Now, Mrs. Bobic, I'd like to first take you to the matter of being taken from your house to Mr. Nogic's, and you were asked questions by two Defence counsels on this matter, both by Defence counsel for Blagoje Simic and Defence counsel for Mr. Tadic. I would like to read you -- you were read different parts of your statement by Defence counsel for Mr. Blagoje Simic, and I'd just like to put to you some of the other things you said about -- that he didn't put to you. Now, this is your statement from 2002. I'm afraid I can't tell you exactly the direct paragraph, because I think we've established there was a change in paragraph numbers. But the statement records you as saying: "Two days after they had searched for weapons, a Serb policeman came to our house and told us we could not stay and we should go to a shelter."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please slow down.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: "Two days after they had searched for weapons, a Serb policeman came to our house and told us that we could not stay and we should go to a shelter." I think that was read to you by Defence counsel for Mr. Blagoje Simic. It goes on to say: "I did not recognise the Serb policeman, but he was accompanied by Vlajko Tadic, Miro's brother. He introduced himself as a police officer. We were not told why we had to leave. We were just told we had to go. We couldn't refuse. We were Muslim. He was armed. We had no choice. We did not want to leave. I had to. We took nothing with us. All of us - myself, my husband, Bedrudin, my sister, and her three children - went. They escorted us to the house. We could not go by ourselves. I was very frightened and nervous, being kicked out of my house. We were not told anything about how long we would be away, what would happen, or if we would ever be allowed to return." Do you recall saying that earlier this year? And is it an accurate description of the circumstances in which you were removed from your house to Idriz Nogic's?

utterances.speaker: EDIBA BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Idriz Nogic's house, I think you've also said in the statement, is located very close to your house; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EDIBA BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There was just a fence between us.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: So in other words, you weren't moved somewhere else in the city to a shelter; you were simply gathered in a location with other non-Serbs, close to your own house. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: EDIBA BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Defence counsel said to you that shelters were marked. Was your -- was this basement or hen house, I think you've described it as, marked as a shelter?

utterances.speaker: EDIBA BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: On the street that you used to live on in Bosanski Samac, were there -- I withdraw that. Let me rephrase it. Between your house on your street and the Spomen Dom, were there also places or apartments occupied by Serb families?

utterances.speaker: EDIBA BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There weren't many, but there were, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And I think you've testified, both in examination-in-chief and cross, that all the families were -- between those locations were gathered up. Were any of the Serb families brought down to stay with you in Idriz Nogic's basement or hen house?

utterances.speaker: EDIBA BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There was just Gordana Nogic there, because she was the wife of Mesud Nogic, and she was in the shelter there with us. She spent two days there and then she left.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: So it was just Muslims and Croats in an unmarked basement, in fact, very close to where your house was?

utterances.speaker: EDIBA BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: I want to also ask you a second question. It's just to clarify the record. And again, it came in the questions posed to you by Defence counsel for Blagoje Simic. You said that your husband used to play chess with Vojin Simic. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EDIBA BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me tell you: Mr. Vojin Simic, Kosta, Cvijan, Sarkan, those are the people who played chess with my husband, as he did. The team that played chess for Bosanski Samac is well known.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. So -- and Vojin Simic is the father of Milan Simic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EDIBA BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And when you went to the municipal building in 1993, it was Blagoje Simic you saw, not Milan Simic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EDIBA BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Of Blagoje Simic. I didn't see Milan, because he was in the wheelchair and he was absent. He was not in Samac.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And the person you met is the Blagoje Simic that you identified to the Chamber yesterday morning. Is that the same person that you say that you met?

utterances.speaker: EDIBA BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. He's sitting here. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. Counsel for Blagoje Simic also then asked you questions about your statement relating to things you had said about having electricity and water, and you said that you had had electricity and water and that later that was cut off and you didn't have any of it. Mr. -- counsel did not proceed then to ask you about the telephones. I'm going to quote to you from your statement from May 2002 that comes after you spoke about the electricity. You say: "There was no electricity, and we had no telephone either. As far as we knew, it was only non-Serbs who had their phones turned off. We heard that the Serbs could still make telephone calls. It was only non-Serb houses where the phone was turned off." Is that an accurate recollection of the situation regarding the telephone facilities in Bosanski Samac after the 17th of April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: EDIBA BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And to your recollection, there were Serb neighbours you knew who had telephone communication, but the non-Serbs did not have telephone communication? I'm sorry, Mrs. Bobic. Did you answer the question?

utterances.speaker: EDIBA BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me for just a second.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Would you like -- did you --

utterances.speaker: EDIBA BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Certainly. I want to know: Is it your recollection that in Bosanski Samac, after the 17th of April, 1992, that you and non-Serbs had no telephone connections but that, in fact, persons of Serb ethnicity did have telephone communication?

utterances.speaker: EDIBA BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everybody else had telephone communication, but Muslims and Croats did not.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. The next topic relates to the issue of humanitarian aid, and again you were asked questions about that by two Defence counsel, one for Blagoje Simic and the other for Mr. Tadic. To Mr. -- to Defence counsel for Blagoje Simic, you explained that, "Everyone had humanitarian aid except for us. It didn't come our way because we were not called when the humanitarian aid was distributed. We knew that it had arrived, because our people were unloading it, but nobody called us when they were distributing that food." And that's at page 61 of yesterday's transcript. What I want to ask is: When you say "our people were unloading it," do you mean that non-Serbs with forced labour assignments were required to unload humanitarian aid as it arrived in Bosanski Samac? Is that what you mean by "our people"?

utterances.speaker: EDIBA BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. I was referring to Muslims and Croats who performed forced labour.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And in your recollection, you received humanitarian aid just once in the first four days when you got some milk and bread; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EDIBA BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And I think you testified once that when you were in the PIK factory, you were given some flour by a gentleman. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: EDIBA BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: So -- and that is the full extent to which you received any form of official humanitarian aid? I'm sorry. Could you repeat your answer. I don't think it was picked up.

utterances.speaker: EDIBA BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And you -- again just ask you: When you say that you knew that it was coming in because people were unloading it, can you give us any idea, if you know - and if you don't, just say it - how often you got the impression or you thought from the information you had about people unloading aid, how often you think that humanitarian arrived -- humanitarian aid arrived in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: EDIBA BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was frequent, but I never received any of it, so I can't tell you how frequently it arrived in Bosanski Samac. The Muslims never got any part of it.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. Again, I want to clear it for the record: Mr. Tadic -- sorry, Defence counsel for Mr. Tadic asked you about a paragraph in your statement, where you explain how people were rounded up and taken to Zasavica and where you said that you also were rounded up in the truck but you had got off the truck. In the draft statement I have, it says that you got off the truck whilst they were not looking. Is that what happened? Was it that they -- and I think you perhaps went on to explain, but the people guarding you had not -- didn't see you get off the truck and you went back in your house and hid?

utterances.speaker: EDIBA BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is how it was: People, civilians living in my street, were loaded on the truck, and then when these men went into another yard that was a bit away, I got off the truck and I hid in the house. I never got back on the truck. I wanted to wait for my son to come back home from his work obligation, because otherwise he would have been surprised to come home and not find me there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't have an objection to this question or answer. All I want to do is to clarify that my question pertained to paragraph 44 of the draft version, which said: "I got off the truck. I came back home. I wanted to wait for my son to come back home from the work obligation." In the statement that I have, in the version that I have, it doesn't say anywhere that the people who were rounding up people went into another yard.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, they went to Zasavica. You omitted the word that should have been in there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mrs. Bobic, you're not supposed to answer anything. Counsel is addressing the Trial Chamber. So please do not interrupt counsel.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: I can confirm that it doesn't contain in the statement about the people going into a yard. It just contains the words "while they weren't looking."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: What did you say? What does the statement contain?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: The statement contains the phrase: "Whilst they were collecting other people from the street and they were not looking, I got off the truck." And I don't think that part of it was in -- was on the record yesterday. So -- but I fully accept Mr. Lukic is right. It doesn't say anything about them going into yards.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. Then you can proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And Defence counsel also asked you to confirm that you remained in Bosanski Samac and not Zasavica after that, but you didn't have -- your son Bedrudin had not swum across the Sava River in August of 1992, had he?

utterances.speaker: EDIBA BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: But you still performed work duty with women from Zasavica from August 1992 onwards?

utterances.speaker: EDIBA BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Finally, I just want to touch briefly on the topic that was recently raised about your property and the information you provided the Chamber that a person Cvijetin Stevanovic, having taken away your property. You explained to the Trial Chamber yesterday how they came and made you and your son load up your property onto a military vehicle. And it was put to you that you never mentioned the actual name of Cvijetin Stevanovic in your 1995 statement. In your 1995 statement, the one that you signed, there's a paragraph as follows: "Before my exchange, soldiers from the Banja Luka Corps came and took all my things and my furniture from my house. They arrived in a military truck. My son and I had to help load it. One of the them who came told us he was from the Banja Luka Corps. I had to sign a paper saying that I had authorised them to take my furniture and possessions. I did not notice who had issued this document." So although your statement from 1995 is much briefer, you did tell officers from the OTP about people coming and taking away your furniture and your possessions?

utterances.speaker: EDIBA BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And you remember --

utterances.speaker: EDIBA BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know his name.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: I'd like to show the witness a document that could perhaps be marked for identification, because I think the next witness will be able to provide more information upon it. But Defence counsel seemed to have made an issue with it with this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. What is the document?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: The document is a power of attorney for Cvijetin Stevanovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Was it signed by this witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. It's signed by her husband. That's why I only want it for ID. I wasn't going to introduce it, but the witness -- the Defence counsel have raised all these questions about her not mentioning his name and issues like that. I simply want to ask her if she recognizes the document, have it marked for ID, and explain where she was later able to provide the name of the exact name of the man who came to take away her property. And I would only have it marked for ID. I think it makes more sense for the next witness, who is the signatory of the document, to actually explain the full circumstances to the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Can we have it marked for identification only?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. It will be P135 ter ID and P135 ID. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: I don't know if you can read that document. Can you have a look at that document in front of you, Mrs. Bobic, and just tell me if you recognise it. Have you seen that document before?

utterances.speaker: EDIBA BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly. I saw this document when my husband was exchanged in Orasje, but that was already in 1994 or 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: But this document says that -- well, it's a power of attorney and it's got the name at the top, Cvijetin Stevanovic. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: EDIBA BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And is it from this document that you were able to put together the pieces of what had happened when you were taken to Batkovici to see Kemal and when they then later came on a military truck and took away all your possessions?

utterances.speaker: EDIBA BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: When you say "no" --

utterances.speaker: EDIBA BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know everything, and I can confirm everything, which is what I'm doing. This is why I came here.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: EDIBA BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But it is better for my husband to do that --

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: EDIBA BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- when he comes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: That's fine. Perhaps you could just hand the document back, Mrs. Bobic.

utterances.speaker: EDIBA BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I repeated this already many times.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: I have just one or two more questions. Defence counsel for Mr. Tadic this morning asked you about proceedings for your property, and he talked about the date July 1993. In July 1993, your husband, Kemal, was in Batkovici; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EDIBA BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: In July 1993, your sister, Amira was imprisoned in Zasavica; is that right?

utterances.speaker: EDIBA BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just to avoid any confusion: I asked two questions pertaining to 1993. One of them was whether in July of 1993 a part of real estate was gifted away to Gordana Pavlovic; and the second question was whether in 1993 this witness initiated proceedings for restitution of property. But I didn't mention the month, because I didn't know which month it was. And when the Prosecutor is asking questions about 1993, I don't know to which of these two items these questions pertained, whether the first one or the second one, because on the second occasion I didn't mention the month, just the year of 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour. Can I just check the transcript?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Okay. Your Honour, I think that there was a question about: Did you know that your husband and your sister initiated proceedings in July 1993? But I'm happy just to talk about 1993 in general, then, because it, in fact, makes no difference.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: In 1993, Kemal was in Batkovici, is that correct, throughout 1993?

utterances.speaker: EDIBA BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And throughout 1993 until --

utterances.speaker: EDIBA BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1994 as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And throughout 1993 until the very end of 1993, your sister, Amira, was in Zasavica; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EDIBA BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. Finally, Mrs. Bobic, one last thing: In -- there was an incident brought up, but I don't want to dwell on it, but there was an incident in 1997 [sic] where your brother-in-law was injured. Was that a kitchen accident where you were both preparing cevapi and pita bread in the kitchen of your establishment?

utterances.speaker: EDIBA BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is how it happened: He was a large man. Shall I explain?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: No, Mrs. Bobic. Don't worry. It's not important. I just want to clarify that that was the circumstances. You were both cooking in the kitchen and this accident occurred.

utterances.speaker: EDIBA BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was just an accident.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Yes. And your husband's brother continued to live with you or live near you and work with you in the restaurant after this accident?

utterances.speaker: EDIBA BOBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: That's the last of my questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I just see page 31, paragraph 14, just for the record, it was an incident in 1987, not 1997, and I don't know if the transcript or my own distinction, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. It should be corrected to 1987.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: That's correct. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mrs. Bobic, for giving evidence to the Tribunal. You are now free to leave the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, according to our practice so far, maybe the defendants should change places.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I was being reminded by Judge Williams here, and I was wondering, in view of the evidence of the previous witness. So how do you want them to sit?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Just in a different way than they are sitting now. I mean, it's not important.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. The accused persons can exchange seats.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, maybe in order to improve this method of identification, maybe one of the Defence counsel can sit in front, just to see -- I mean to have -- I mean, too simple, Your Honour, to have three persons here. I mean --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, most of the evidence shows that most of the Prosecution witnesses lived in Bosanski Samac, they know, and there is very little value in courtroom identification. So I don't think it's necessary to go to any unreasonable lengths.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Can the witness make the solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you. Please sit down. Yes, Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you, Your Honour

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Mr. Bobic, in the five minutes that we've got before the morning break, I'll just go through some introductory matters. You were born in Bosanski Samac in 1940, I believe?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And you went to school there, both primary school, secondary school?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: When you're answering the questions, speak up a bit, because they have to be recorded so everyone can hear, and they have to be heard so that they can be interpreted. So you can -- feel free to move the chair in and relax, but keep your voice up so that everything can be recorded. Because you're going to be sitting there for a while, so just get used to it. You married, I think, in 1969, the previous witness, Ediba Bobic.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Indeed, you and your brother married Ediba and her sister?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did you train as a chef in Brcko and as a baker in Orasje?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC
utterances.text: Yes, but in fact I went to vocational, secondary school, and there I trained as a baker. And then in Orasje, I trained as a chef, and in Brcko as a butcher. So I have three trades.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. Are you a Muslim by ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: You had, in early 1992, two children, I believe, two sons, one of whom was unfortunately killed in February of that year; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: I'd just like to get a brief overview of your occupation and businesses in Bosanski Samac. Did you have a general store there called Ideal, or Ideal?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And was that held in the name of your niece, Nermina?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: In addition, did you have a pharmacy or natural health and herb shop which was --

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. A herbal pharmacy, pharmacy selling herbal remedies.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. And was that in the name of one of your sons, Enver?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: In addition, did you own a video rental shop?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And finally, did you also own a cafe called Sedrvan?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC
utterances.text: Yes. Unfortunately, it was destroyed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: So essentially, in April of 1992, you were involved in four businesses, the ones that I've mentioned to you?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, it's 10.29. I'm going to move on to his political background. Would you like to have the break now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I think we can take our break now and continue the proceedings at 1100 hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The Prosecution continues examination-in-chief. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: In 1991, did you join the SDA?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And did you achieve any rank in the structure of the party?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC
utterances.text: Yes. I was on the board.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Is that the executive board of the party?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Can you recall approximately when you were appointed to the executive board?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC
utterances.text: When the parties were formed, I can't recall the exact date, but it was in 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Mr. Bobic, I notice you have a document in front of you, and I think the Defence counsel and the Court should know what it is. Is that your statement that you have there, by any chance, in B/C/S?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Could you just close it and put it away for the time being, okay? If we need to refer to it, I'll certainly ask you about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Could we just know -- because there are at least two statements, of which statement you are speaking now, so that we can follow? MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. I believe it was the statement prepared in anticipation of the 92 bis -- being used as a 92 bis document. It remains, however, unsigned and not officially adopted. But that's the document that the witness would have had in front of him, I believe. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: The only reason I told you that, Mr. Bobic, is that we prefer to hear your statement orally rather than by reference to that document. That's all. And do you continue to retain membership of the SDA?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did your sons, in particular, your son Enver, hold a position in any affiliated body to the SDA?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC
utterances.text: Yes. My son was the president of the MOS, M-O-S. That's the Muslim Youth Party, which was a part of the SDA.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And did he hold that position in the period of time preceding April of 1992?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you hold your position on the executive board of the SDA in the period of time preceding April of 1992?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you ever run for any other office in the SDA?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: On the 14th of February, 1992, your son was killed in Bosanski Samac, and following that tragic event, did you essentially retire from public life and did you just devote yourself to your work and your family?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And were you essentially going about life in that way as at the 16th and 17th of April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio, I would like some explanation as to what "retiring" means. Did he resign from the position in the political party? MR. DI FAZIO: Very well. I'll clarify that. I'm sorry. It does leave that up in the air.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: The Chamber wants to know exactly what you mean by -- or perhaps what I meant by your retiring from public life. Is it the case that you still continued in -- with membership of the SDA following the event in February of 1992 but that you didn't participate in functions, rallies, activities of the SDA?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC
utterances.text: Yes. I continued being a member of the SDA, and indeed I'm still a member of the party. I do not hold any office. I do not have any function in the political life. But that's my party, a Muslim party, and I have no other party.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: Does that clarify it for Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you. Can the witness be shown D24/2 ter? The document is under seal, I believe. Sorry. Before it is shown to the witness, may I ask -- inquire from the registry whether that document is simply marked for identification at that stage? I thought it was a full exhibit, but I may be wrong. D24/2. Perhaps I'll retract that, then. May the witness be shown D25/4. Can I just see the document before it's presented? Yes. I do apologise to the Chamber and to the registry. We need the B/C/S version of the document to be shown to the witness. That's the English. I should have mentioned it was D25/4 ter. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Witness, I'd just like you to have a look at the document that you have before you. I don't want you to study it in detail. I think if you go to three pages from the back, three, yes, three pages from the back, you will find a page at the top of which are the words "supplies section." Would you please find that. Three pages from the back.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: If the defendants -- if the Defence counsel want it on the ELMO, I'll put it on the ELMO. Thank you. Perhaps it could be placed on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Just a few questions on this document, please. Number 2 is Bobic; that's your surname. Look at the number next to it, 62-642. Was that your home telephone number in April of 1992?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: It says "supplies section." The document speaks for itself. You can see who the commander is, who is in reserve. Presumably there are telephone numbers there and the names of other men who were presumably members of this body. Are you aware of the existence of anything called the supplies section within the SDA?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Were you aware of ever having been placed on this list?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Were you ever even consulted about being placed on -- as a member of something called a supplies section?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: I'm done with the document. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: I'd like to ask you some questions about some names. Do you know Simo Zaric?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: How long would you say that you have known him?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC
utterances.text: I've known him for maybe 30 years.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And do you know Miroslav Tadic?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And how long have you known him?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC
utterances.text: The same.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Do you know Blagoje Simic?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC
utterances.text: Yes, Dr. Blagoje Simic. I do know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did you ever see -- speak to him in a professional capacity?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC
utterances.text: No. We were not that close, but we did see each other in the town sometimes. I also know his brother Cedo.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. Look around the room and see if you can identify those men, please.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC
utterances.text: Simo Zaric, Blagoje Simic, Miro Tadic, nicknamed Brko.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: The witness indicated the sequence of the defendants, using his hands, if Your Honours please, and I think that's sufficient for the record that he correctly identified the defendants.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Do we need to say, Mr. Di Fazio, going from the right to the left? MR. DI FAZIO: That would -- yes, that would clarify the matter and seal it finally. Thank you, if Your Honours please, and that that is indeed the position in which they're seated.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: I want you to turn your mind to the events of the night of the 16th and 17th of April. There's no question that on that night hostilities broke out in Bosanski Samac. Were you at home on that night?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did you hear the sound of gunfire and that sort of thing?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did you go outside at any time during the night?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC
utterances.text: Yes, into my yard.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: What was your address at the time, that is, on the 16th and 17th of April, 1992? What number, what street did you live in in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC
utterances.text: Ivo Lola Ribar Street number 14/12.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: How long had you lived there?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC
utterances.text: From the day when I was born. I was born in my father's house, and then I built my own house, but that was in 1975. I built it in the same position.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. And as long as you had lived there, had the street always been called Ivo Lola Ribar Street?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: What's it called nowadays?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC
utterances.text: Draza Mihajlovic Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Now, you said that in the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Perhaps we may know when the name changed. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Have you any idea when the change of name took place?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC
utterances.text: All the street names in Samac have been changed. Tito Street is now called Karadjordje Street.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I just want to find out: Is it after 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Let's turn to your foray outside into the yard. Did you see anything when you went outside?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd just like to get an idea of the circumstances. About what time of the night was it?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC
utterances.text: At around 1.00 a.m.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Can you tell the Chamber if there was any street lighting in the vicinity of where you were standing?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC
utterances.text: Yes. It's an intersection, and there is a very strong light there. That's where my house is.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you proceed to tell the Chamber now what you saw when you went outside?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC
utterances.text: When I got out into my yard, the house across the street, owned by Belkisa, somebody said from there, "Bobic, go back. Go back in." I was -- I lay down into the flowers, flower bed that was there, and I saw Fadil Topcagic leading about 10 or 12 men there. There was Lugar there, also Tralja. I met him later on, and that's why I knew him. And they passed me by at a distance of maybe three or four metres, and they went on into the intersection. And there was shooting going on from the direction of the stadium. I went back into my home, and that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. I take it that at the time you didn't know who Lugar and Tralja and these other men were. Did you, unfortunately, in subsequent weeks, become acquainted with them?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you remain inside your house for the rest of the night?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC
utterances.text: Yes. A colleague of mine called me, Vlado Sarkanovic, and he said that Samac fell and that I shouldn't go anywhere. And I remained at home and didn't go anywhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you receive any news as to what had happened via the radio?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC
utterances.text: Yes. They said, in the morning, at around 10.00 a.m. or maybe 9.30, that Samac now belonged to Serbs and that the population shouldn't congregate in groups and that they should be wearing white cloths or scarves, and that's about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. Were those instructions issued to all the population?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC
utterances.text: Yes. For the non-Serb population, Croats and Muslims.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. It's a little bit confusing, page 43, line 16. Maybe I'm wrong, but when the witness mentioned white clothes and scarves, in fact, in B/C/S language, he said bandannas, marame. MR. DI FAZIO: I'll clarify that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Now you made it clear that the instructions were directed to the non-Serb population. Defence counsel would also like you to, if you can, tell the Chamber what the instructions were as to the white items that had to be worn. Can you remember that with any more clarity?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC
utterances.text: That they should be placed around one's arm, like this, over the right arm, like this.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, the witness demonstrates with a white tissue placed on his upper-right arm.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: In the days that followed, did the tele -- well, perhaps not in the days that followed, but indeed on that day, the 17th, and in subsequent days, did you continue to have use of your telephone?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC
utterances.text: Yes, for a few days, and then all the Muslims and Croats were disconnected. Only Serbs had telephone lines, because they had the post office in their hands. They took all the vital communications, the post office, the municipality, the courthouse, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell the Chamber how it is that you know that the Serbs still retained their telephone lines? How can you make -- how can you say that? With what authority can you make that assertion?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC
utterances.text: Because we no longer had the communications. I communicated with my neighbours, and one could only communicate from a Serb house. You had to go to a Serb if you wanted to call anyone in Brcko, and they in fact did accommodate us. They did allow us to make phone calls.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know a gentleman named Miroslav Rakic, also known as Celo?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Do you know another fellow, Dragan Tubonjic, also known as Tubonja?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC
utterances.text: Yes. He's from Samac, and the former is a police officer from Odzak. So Rakic is from Odzak, and Tubonjic is from Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you see them in the period of time following the 16th and 17th of April?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC
utterances.text: Yes. They came to my house and they said that there was a sniper upstairs, and I told him, "Please be my guest." They went upstairs, didn't find anything, and then went back downstairs, had coffee with me. Tubonja took my brother's hunting rifle and took it with him. He did not give me any documents. It was a trophy weapon that belonged to my brother. He used to be a huntsman. He had died previously, and his son Nermin inherited the rifle. He took the rifle as a trophy, and the firing pin had been filed away in the SUP previously. So they just kept the weapon as a trophy.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: For the purposes of the Chamber, is it the case that the removal of the firing pin completely disables the weapon?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC
utterances.text: Yes. It is no longer functional. It's just like a picture on the wall.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Indeed, is that where it was kept, up on the wall, as a trophy?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. These two fellows, Rakic and Tubonjic, were they members of the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC
utterances.text: Well, I couldn't really say that, because I don't know. Things that I don't know, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. Please don't tell us something if you don't know. If you don't know something, make that clear. Were they policemen working in Bosanski Samac? One of them was from Odzak, but what about the other one?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC
utterances.text: No. He still hadn't completed his education, and at that time I did some work for the school, and that's why I know that very well, that he was still going to school.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: With what authority did they come into your house and take away your brother's trophy? Did they ever say that they were acting on instructions, with authority, that they held any particular position? Can you recall anything? If you can't recall, say so, but if you can recall anything that they said to indicate with what backing they came to seize the weapon, please let us know.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC
utterances.text: Yes. They said that they had to take that to SUP, and they never brought it back. That was the intention with which they had come.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you understand them to be acting on behalf of the SUP, on behalf of police from the SUP?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Okay. In subsequent days, did you move from your house to the home of a person nearby, Mesud Nogic?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC
utterances.text: Yes. All of us neighbours were there. Mesud Nogic was there, as was his wife, who is a Serb, Gordana. There were unfortunately two other men there who were killed immediately upon leaving that place. One of them was Hodzic Mirsad, Sead Hurtic, who was killed in Crkvina later. There were other neighbours there. There was a lady Croat with her son, and some other neighbours. It was the safest place for us.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: Would Your Honours just permit me to confer with my colleague, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: How long did you remain there?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC
utterances.text: Since that was right next to my house, we would go back and forth. The war had already started. People were coming from Slavonia. I don't know exactly where from.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC
utterances.text: This was coming from Croatia. The war had broken out and people were hiding in the shelters.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. In the few days following the 16th and 17th of April, did you go to the TO building in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Why did you go there?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC
utterances.text: They made an announcement on the radio that all men from Bosanski Samac who had remained and were non-Serbs, meaning Croats or Muslims, should report. And we went there to have our names recorded. They asked me there where I had served in my mandatory military service. I told them that I was in logistics, I worked in the kitchen. And then they asked who was a member of the anti-rocket units, who was in an anti-sabotage unit, in the tank unit, and so on. The people who had been in the communication unit, the signalmen, fared the worst. It was just a list of Muslim and Croat men, referring to where they had served in the military service and at which time period.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. You said in your answer that people who had been in the communications unit fared the worst. Are you there referring to what happened to them subsequently in prisons in the -- in and around Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. I take it from your answer that you are aware of what the men, the Muslims and Croats who accompanied you to the TO, were asked as well?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC
utterances.text: After having asked us where we had served, they told us to go back to our homes, and we went home without any fear. They let us go and we went home. That's what happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Okay. That's fine. All I'm interested in is this: You've indicated two areas that they were interested in, one is who you were, what your name was; and secondly, what you did in the course of your military service. Is that a correct position?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Other than those two areas, were there any other inquiries about anything else?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC
utterances.text: No, there were no more inquiries.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: You were arrested, I believe, on the 23rd of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. Up until that time, that is, between the 16th and 17th of April and the 23rd of May, 1992, when you were arrested, did you see your son performing any labour or forced labour?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC
utterances.text: Yes. All of them went to perform labour, not just my son. All of them went. They went to the PIK factory. They also went to work in the fields. They did all kinds of jobs.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. When you say "all of them," who do you mean?

utterances.speaker: KEMAL BOBIC
